sanskrit: svayaṃ śāṃtanavo rājann abhyadhāvad dhanaṃjayam pragṛhya kārmukaṃ ghoraṃ kāladaṇḍopamaṃ raṇe
english: The son of Śantanu himself, O king, charged upon Dhanaṃjaya in the battle, gripping his dreadful bow that was like the rod of Death.

sanskrit: arjuno 'pi dhanur gṛhya gāṇḍīvaṃ lokaviśrutam abhyadhāvata tejasvī gāṅgeyaṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Arjuna too, the radiant one, seizing his bow Gāṇḍīva renowned throughout the world, rushed against the son of Gaṅgā at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau kuruśārdūlau parasparavadhaiṣiṇau gāṅgeyas tu raṇe pārthaṃ viddhvā nākampayad balī tathaiva pāṇḍavo rājan bhīṣmaṃ nākampayad yudhi
english: Those two tigers among the Kurus each sought to slay the other; yet the mighty son of Gaṅgā, though he pierced Pārtha in the fight, could not make him waver, and likewise, O king, the son of Pāṇḍu could not make Bhīṣma waver in the battle.

sanskrit: sātyakiś ca maheṣvāsaḥ kṛtavarmāṇam abhyayāt tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: And Sātyaki, the great archer, advanced upon Kṛtavarman; between those two there arose a tumultuous, hair-raising combat.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ kṛtavarmā ca sātyakim ānarchatuḥ śarair ghorais takṣamāṇau parasparam
english: Sātyaki assailed Kṛtavarman and Kṛtavarman Sātyaki, the two of them mangling each other with terrible arrows.

sanskrit: tau śarācitasarvāṅgau śuśubhāte mahābalau vasante puṣpaśabalau puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Their every limb studded with arrows, those two mighty warriors shone like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in springtime, dappled and bright with blossoms in flower.

sanskrit: abhimanyur maheṣvāso bṛhadbalam ayodhayat tataḥ kosalako rājā saubhadrasya viśāṃ pate dhvajaṃ ciccheda samare sārathiṃ ca nyapātayat
english: Abhimanyu, the great archer, gave battle to Bṛhadbala; thereupon, O lord of peoples, the king of Kosala cut down in the fight the banner of Subhadrā's son and felled his charioteer.

sanskrit: saubhadras tu tataḥ kruddhaḥ pātite rathasārathau bṛhadbalaṃ mahārāja vivyādha navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then the son of Subhadrā, enraged at the slaying of his charioteer, pierced Bṛhadbala, O great king, with nine arrows.

sanskrit: athāparābhyāṃ bhallābhyāṃ pītābhyām arimardanaḥ dhvajam ekena ciccheda pārṣṇim ekena sārathim anyonyaṃ ca śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kruddhau rājaṃs tatakṣatuḥ
english: Then with two more broad-headed shafts, golden-hued, that crusher of foes cut the banner with one and the rein-driver with the other; and the two of them, enraged, O king, mangled each other with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: māninaṃ samare dṛptaṃ kṛtavairaṃ mahāratham bhīmasenas tava sutaṃ duryodhanam ayodhayat
english: Proud, insolent in battle, a great car-warrior who had earned his enmity—such was your son Duryodhana, whom Bhīmasena now engaged.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau naraśārdūlau kurumukhyau mahābalau anyonyaṃ śaravarṣābhyāṃ vavṛṣāte raṇājire
english: Those two tigers among men, foremost of the Kurus, mighty in strength, rained upon each other showers of arrows on the field of battle.

sanskrit: tau tu vīkṣya mahātmānau kṛtinau citrayodhinau vismayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ samapadyata bhārata
english: Beholding those two great-souled and accomplished warriors, masters of the wondrous arts of combat, amazement seized all beings, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu nakulaṃ pratyudyāya mahāratham avidhyan niśitair bāṇair bahubhir marmabhedibhiḥ
english: Duḥśāsana, advancing against the great car-warrior Nakula, struck him with many whetted arrows that pierced to the vitals.

sanskrit: tasya mādrīsutaḥ ketuṃ saśaraṃ ca śarāsanam ciccheda niśitair bāṇaiḥ prahasann iva bhārata athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samārdayat
english: The son of Mādrī, as if laughing, cut apart with sharp arrows his standard and his bow together with its shaft, O descendant of Bharata; and then he tormented him with twenty-five small darts.

sanskrit: putras tu tava durdharṣo nakulasya mahāhave yugeṣāṃ cicchide bāṇair dhvajaṃ caiva nyapātayat
english: But your son, hard to assail, in that great battle cut with his arrows the yoke-pole of Nakula's car and brought down his banner as well.

sanskrit: durmukhaḥ sahadevaṃ tu pratyudyāya mahābalam vivyādha śaravarṣeṇa yatamānaṃ mahāhave
english: Durmukha, advancing against the mighty Sahadeva, pierced him with a shower of arrows as he strove in the great battle.

sanskrit: sahadevas tato vīro durmukhasya mahāhave śareṇa bhṛśatīkṣṇena pātayām āsa sārathim
english: Then the hero Sahadeva, in that great battle, with an exceedingly sharp arrow brought down Durmukha's charioteer.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samāsādya samare yuddhadurmadau trāsayetāṃ śarair ghoraiḥ kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau
english: Closing upon each other in the fight, those two, frenzied for combat and bent on stroke and counter-stroke, terrified one another with terrible arrows.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ svayaṃ rājā madrarājānam abhyayāt tasya madrādhipaś cāpaṃ dvidhā ciccheda māriṣa
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira himself advanced against the king of the Madras; and the lord of the Madras cut his bow in two, O venerable one.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ anyat kārmukam ādāya vegavad balavattaram
english: Casting aside that severed bow, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī took up another, swifter and stronger.

sanskrit: tato madreśvaraṃ rājā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ chādayām āsa saṃkruddhas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then the king, enraged, covered the lord of the Madras with smooth-jointed arrows and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tato droṇam abhyadravata bhārata tasya droṇaḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ parāsukaraṇaṃ dṛḍham tridhā ciccheda samare yatamānasya kārmukam
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna rushed upon Droṇa, O descendant of Bharata; but Droṇa, greatly enraged, cut into three pieces in the fight his stout bow—the very life-taker—as he strove with it.

sanskrit: śaraṃ caiva mahāghoraṃ kāladaṇḍam ivāparam preṣayām āsa samare so 'sya kāye nyamajjata
english: And he loosed in the battle a most dreadful arrow, like a second rod of Death, which sank deep into his body.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sāyakāṃś ca caturdaśa droṇaṃ drupadaputras tu prativivyādha saṃyuge tāv anyonyaṃ susaṃkruddhau cakratuḥ subhṛśaṃ raṇam
english: Then taking up another bow and fourteen arrows, the son of Drupada pierced Droṇa in return in that engagement; and the two of them, greatly enraged, waged a most furious combat against each other.

sanskrit: saumadattiṃ raṇe śaṅkho rabhasaṃ rabhaso yudhi pratyudyayau mahārāja tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: In the fight Śaṅkha, the impetuous, advanced against the impetuous son of Somadatta, O great king, crying, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: tasya vai dakṣiṇaṃ vīro nirbibheda raṇe bhujam saumadattis tathā śaṅkhaṃ jatrudeśe samāhanat
english: The hero pierced his right arm in the fight; and the son of Somadatta in turn struck Śaṅkha in the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate dṛptayoḥ samare tūrṇaṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: Between those two, proud and swift in battle, O lord of peoples, there arose a combat of terrible form, like that between Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: bāhlīkaṃ tu raṇe kruddhaṃ kruddharūpo viśāṃ pate abhyadravad ameyātmā dhṛṣṭaketur mahārathaḥ
english: Against Bāhlīka, enraged in the fight, the immeasurable-souled Dhṛṣṭaketu, that great car-warrior, fierce of aspect, charged, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: bāhlīkas tu tato rājan dhṛṣṭaketum amarṣaṇam śarair bahubhir ānarchat siṃhanādam athānadat
english: Then Bāhlīka, O king, assailed the indignant Dhṛṣṭaketu with many arrows and let forth a lion's roar.

sanskrit: cedirājas tu saṃkruddho bāhlīkaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha samare tūrṇaṃ matto mattam iva dvipam
english: But the king of the Cedis, greatly enraged, swiftly pierced Bāhlīka in the fight with nine arrows, as a rutting elephant assails another in rut.

sanskrit: tau tatra samare kruddhau nardantau ca muhur muhuḥ samīyatuḥ susaṃkruddhāv aṅgārakabudhāv iva
english: There in the fight those two, enraged and roaring again and again, came together in fury like Mars and Mercury.

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ krūrakarmā ghaṭotkacaḥ alambusaṃ pratyudiyād balaṃ śakra ivāhave
english: Against the rākṣasa Alambuṣa, cruel in his deeds, the cruel-deeded Ghaṭotkaca advanced in battle, as Śakra against Bala.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tu saṃkruddho rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahābalam navatyā sāyakais tīkṣṇair dārayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, greatly enraged, rent that mighty rākṣasa with ninety sharp arrows, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: alambusas tu samare bhaimaseniṃ mahābalam bahudhā vārayām āsa śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: But Alambuṣa in the fight again and again held off the mighty son of Bhīmasena with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: vyabhrājetāṃ tatas tau tu saṃyuge śaravikṣatau yathā devāsure yuddhe balaśakrau mahābalau
english: Wounded by arrows, those two then shone in the engagement like the mighty Bala and Śakra in the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī samare rājan drauṇim abhyudyayau balī aśvatthāmā tataḥ kruddhaḥ śikhaṇḍinam avasthitam
english: The mighty Śikhaṇḍin in the fight advanced against the son of Droṇa, O king; thereupon Aśvatthāman, enraged, struck Śikhaṇḍin as he stood firm.

sanskrit: nārācena sutīkṣṇena bhṛśaṃ viddhvā vyakampayat śikhaṇḍy api tato rājan droṇaputram atāḍayat
english: Piercing him grievously with a keen iron shaft, he made him quake; yet Śikhaṇḍin too, O king, then smote the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sāyakena supītena tīkṣṇena niśitena ca tau jaghnatus tadānyonyaṃ śarair bahuvidhair mṛdhe
english: With a fine, sharp, well-whetted arrow he struck him; and the two of them then smote each other in the fray with manifold arrows.

sanskrit: bhagadattaṃ raṇe śūraṃ virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ abhyayāt tvarito rājaṃs tato yuddham avartata
english: Against the valiant Bhagadatta in the fight, Virāṭa the commander of hosts advanced in haste, O king; and thereupon a battle arose between them.

sanskrit: virāṭo bhagadattena śaravarṣeṇa tāḍitaḥ abhyavarṣat susaṃkruddho megho vṛṣṭyā ivācalam
english: Virāṭa, struck by Bhagadatta with a shower of arrows, greatly enraged, rained upon him in return, as a cloud pours its rain upon a mountain.

sanskrit: bhagadattas tatas tūrṇaṃ virāṭaṃ pṛthivīpatim chādayām āsa samare meghaḥ sūryam ivoditam
english: Then Bhagadatta swiftly covered Virāṭa, lord of the earth, in the fight, as a cloud covers the risen sun.

sanskrit: bṛhatkṣatraṃ tu kaikeyaṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvato yayau taṃ kṛpaḥ śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa bhārata
english: Against Bṛhatkṣatra the Kaikeya, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat advanced; and Kṛpa covered him with a shower of arrows, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: gautamaṃ kekayaḥ kruddhaḥ śaravṛṣṭyābhyapūrayat tāv anyonyaṃ hayān hatvā dhanuṣī vinikṛtya vai
english: The Kekaya, enraged, overwhelmed the son of Gautama with a downpour of arrows; and the two, having slain each other's horses and cut apart each other's bows—

sanskrit: virathāv asiyuddhāya samīyatur amarṣaṇau tayos tad abhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ sudāruṇam
english: Bereft of their cars, the indignant pair came together for combat with swords; and between them there arose a battle of terrible form, most fierce.

sanskrit: drupadas tu tato rājā saindhavaṃ vai jayadratham abhyudyayau saṃprahṛṣṭo hṛṣṭarūpaṃ paraṃtapa
english: Then King Drupada, full of gladness, advanced against the gladsome Jayadratha, lord of the Sindhus, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tataḥ saindhavako rājā drupadaṃ viśikhais tribhiḥ tāḍayām āsa samare sa ca taṃ pratyavidhyata
english: Then the king of the Sindhus struck Drupada in the fight with three arrows, and Drupada pierced him in return.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ sudāruṇam īkṣitṛprītijananaṃ śukrāṅgārakayor iva
english: Between them there arose a battle of terrible form, most fierce, delighting the beholders, like that between Venus and Mars.

sanskrit: vikarṇas tu sutas tubhyaṃ sutasomaṃ mahābalam abhyayāj javanair aśvais tato yuddham avartata
english: Your son Vikarṇa advanced with swift horses against the mighty Sutasoma; and thereupon a battle arose.

sanskrit: vikarṇaḥ sutasomaṃ tu viddhvā nākampayac charaiḥ sutasomo vikarṇaṃ ca tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Vikarṇa, though he pierced Sutasoma with arrows, could not make him waver; and neither could Sutasoma make Vikarṇa waver—and that was a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: suśarmāṇaṃ naravyāghraṃ cekitāno mahārathaḥ abhyadravat susaṃkruddhaḥ pāṇḍavārthe parākramī
english: Against Suśarman, that tiger among men, the great car-warrior Cekitāna, valorous and greatly enraged, charged for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: suśarmā tu mahārāja cekitānaṃ mahāratham mahatā śaravarṣeṇa vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: But Suśarman, O great king, held off the great car-warrior Cekitāna in the engagement with a vast shower of arrows.

sanskrit: cekitāno 'pi saṃrabdhaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ mahāhave prācchādayat tam iṣubhir mahāmegha ivācalam
english: Cekitāna too, in fury, covered Suśarman in that great battle with arrows, as a great cloud covers a mountain.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ prativindhyaṃ tu parākrāntaṃ parākramī abhyadravata rājendra matto mattam iva dvipam
english: Śakuni, the valorous, charged against the valiant Prativindhya, O lord of kings, as a rutting elephant against another in rut.

sanskrit: yaudhiṣṭhiras tu saṃkruddhaḥ saubalaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vyadārayata saṃgrāme maghavān iva dānavam
english: But the son of Yudhiṣṭhira, greatly enraged, rent the son of Subala in the fight with sharp arrows, as Maghavat rends a dānava.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ prativindhyaṃ tu pratividhyantam āhave vyadārayan mahāprājñaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And Śakuni, the highly sagacious, rent Prativindhya, who was piercing him in return in the battle, with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇaṃ tu rājendra kāmbojānāṃ mahāratham śrutakarmā parākrāntam abhyadravata saṃyuge
english: Against Sudakṣiṇa, O lord of kings, the valiant great car-warrior of the Kāmbojas, Śrutakarman charged in the engagement.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇas tu samare sāhadeviṃ mahāratham viddhvā nākampayata vai mainākam iva parvatam
english: But Sudakṣiṇa in the fight, though he pierced the great car-warrior son of Sahadeva, could not make him waver, any more than the mountain Maināka.

sanskrit: śrutakarmā tataḥ kruddhaḥ kāmbojānāṃ mahāratham śarair bahubhir ānarchad dārayann iva sarvaśaḥ
english: Then Śrutakarman, enraged, assailed the great car-warrior of the Kāmbojas with many arrows, rending him, as it were, on every side.

sanskrit: irāvān atha saṃkruddhaḥ śrutāyuṣam amarṣaṇam pratyudyayau raṇe yatto yattarūpataraṃ tataḥ
english: Then Irāvān, greatly enraged and on his guard, advanced in the fight against the indignant Śrutāyus, who was yet more on his guard.

sanskrit: ārjunis tasya samare hayān hatvā mahārathaḥ nanāda sumahan nādaṃ tat sainyaṃ pratyapūrayat
english: The son of Arjuna, that great car-warrior, having slain his horses in the fight, roared a mighty roar that filled the host.

sanskrit: śrutāyus tv atha saṃkruddhaḥ phālguneḥ samare hayān nijaghāna gadāgreṇa tato yuddham avartata
english: But Śrutāyus, greatly enraged, slew the horses of Phalguna's son in the fight with the head of his mace; and thereupon a battle arose.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kuntibhojaṃ mahāratham sasenaṃ sasutaṃ vīraṃ saṃsasajjatur āhave
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti closed in battle with the great car-warrior Kuntibhoja, that hero, together with his host and his sons.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma āvantyānāṃ parākramam yad ayudhyan sthirā bhūtvā mahatyā senayā saha
english: There we beheld a wondrous feat of valor by the men of Avanti, in that, standing firm, they fought against a mighty host.

sanskrit: anuvindas tu gadayā kuntibhojam atāḍayat kuntibhojas tatas tūrṇaṃ śaravrātair avākirat
english: Anuvinda struck Kuntibhoja with his mace; and Kuntibhoja then swiftly overwhelmed him with volleys of arrows.

sanskrit: kuntibhojasutaś cāpi vindaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ sa ca taṃ prativivyādha tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And the son of Kuntibhoja, too, pierced Vinda with arrows, and Vinda pierced him in return—and that was a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca gāndhārān pañca māriṣa sasainyās te sasainyāṃś ca yodhayām āsur āhave
english: The five Kekaya brothers, with their hosts, gave battle to five Gāndhāras with their hosts, O venerable one.

sanskrit: vīrabāhuś ca te putro vairāṭiṃ rathasattamam uttaraṃ yodhayām āsa vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ uttaraś cāpi taṃ dhīraṃ vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And your son Vīrabāhu gave battle to Uttara, son of Virāṭa, that best of car-warriors, and pierced him with sharp arrows; and Uttara too pierced that steadfast warrior with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: cedirāṭ samare rājann ulūkaṃ samabhidravat ulūkaś cāpi taṃ bāṇair niśitair lomavāhibhiḥ
english: The king of the Cedis in the fight rushed upon Ulūka, O king; and Ulūka too assailed him with sharp, feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ samabhavad ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate dārayetāṃ susaṃkruddhāv anyonyam aparājitau
english: Between them there arose a combat of terrible form, O lord of peoples; greatly enraged and unvanquished, they rent each other.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvaṃdvasahasrāṇi rathavāraṇavājinām padātīnāṃ ca samare tava teṣāṃ ca saṃkulam
english: Thus in thousands of single combats of car-warriors, elephants, horsemen, and foot-soldiers, your forces and theirs grew confounded in the fight.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tad yuddham āsīn madhuradarśanam tata unmattavad rājan na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: For a moment that battle was fair to behold; but thereafter, O king, as in a frenzy, nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: gajo gajena samare rathī ca rathinaṃ yayau aśvo 'śvaṃ samabhipretya padātiś ca padātinam
english: Elephant met elephant in the fight, and car-warrior met car-warrior, horse closed with horse, and foot-soldier with foot-soldier.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ sudurdharṣaṃ vyākulaṃ samapadyata śūrāṇāṃ samare tatra samāsādya parasparam
english: Then a most unbearable and tumultuous battle came about there, as the heroes in the fight closed upon one another.

sanskrit: tatra devarṣayaḥ siddhāś cāraṇāś ca samāgatāḥ praikṣanta tad raṇaṃ ghoraṃ devāsuraraṇopamam
english: There the divine seers, the siddhas, and the cāraṇas, gathered together, gazed upon that terrible battle, like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: tato dantisahasrāṇi rathānāṃ cāpi māriṣa aśvaughāḥ puruṣaughāś ca viparītaṃ samāyayuḥ
english: Then thousands of elephants and of chariots, floods of horses and floods of men, O venerable one, came together in confusion.

sanskrit: tatra tatraiva dṛśyante rathavāraṇapattayaḥ sādinaś ca naravyāghra yudhyamānā muhur muhuḥ
english: Here and there were seen car-warriors, elephants, and foot-soldiers, and horsemen too, O tiger among men, fighting again and again.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājañ śatasahasrāṇi tatra tatra tadā tadā nirmaryādaṃ prayuddhāni tat te vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, hundreds of thousands fought there, here and there, then and again, beyond all bounds; of this I shall tell you, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: na putraḥ pitaraṃ jajñe na pitā putram aurasam na bhrātā bhrātaraṃ tatra svasrīyaṃ na ca mātulaḥ
english: There son knew not father, nor father his own begotten son, nor brother brother, nor uncle his sister's son.

sanskrit: mātulaṃ na ca svasrīyo na sakhāyaṃ sakhā tathā āviṣṭā iva yudhyante pāṇḍavāḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: Nor sister's son his uncle, nor friend his friend; as if possessed, the Pāṇḍavas fought together with the Kurus.

sanskrit: rathānīkaṃ naravyāghrāḥ ke cid abhyapatan rathaiḥ abhajyanta yugair eva yugāni bharatarṣabha
english: Some of those tigers among men hurled themselves with their chariots upon the array of cars, and yoke shattered against yoke, O bull of the Bharatas.
